set.title: Employee Preferences for Workplace Benefits
set.topicCategory: IELTS Academic Task 1 / Grouped bar chart
set.intendedMeaning: The chart compares male and female employees’ selections of six workplace benefits. Women made slightly more selections overall, but preferences differed by benefit.

passages.fully_minimally_corrected:
The bar chart compares the numbers of male and female employees who selected each of six workplace benefits in a survey conducted at a company. The figures represent selections rather than percentages, and respondents could choose more than one option. Overall, flexible working hours attracted the highest number of women, whereas remote work was the most popular choice among men. Childcare showed the widest gender gap, while training and private health insurance produced the most similar figures.
Flexible hours were chosen by 420 women and 360 men. Thus, 60 more women than men selected this benefit, and women outnumbered men by roughly one sixth of the male figure. Remote work displayed the opposite pattern. It attracted 410 men, compared with 390 women, so the male figure exceeded the female figure by only 20. This was the only category in which men's participation was higher by fewer than 30 respondents.
Training was selected by 300 men and 260 women, giving a combined total of 560 selections. The difference between the two groups was 40, and the male figure was approximately 15 per cent higher than the female figure. Private health insurance recorded 340 male selections and 310 female selections. These figures were close to each other, with men accounting for 30 more selections than women.
The greatest contrast appeared in childcare support. As many as 280 women selected this option, compared with just 90 men. The female figure was therefore slightly more than three times the male figure, and women made up about three quarters of the 370 selections in this category. Childcare was also the least popular option among men, although it ranked fourth among women.
Gym membership showed another clear male advantage. A total of 250 men chose it, as opposed to 170 women. In other words, 80 fewer women than men selected the benefit, and the number of men was nearly one and a half times that of women. Nevertheless, gym membership remained less popular overall than flexible hours, remote work, training and private insurance.
Across all six benefits, women made 1,830 selections, while men made 1,750. The women's total was therefore 80 higher than the men's, although the two totals were broadly comparable. Flexible hours and childcare together accounted for more than one third of all female selections. By contrast, remote work and private insurance represented just over two fifths of the male total.
When the categories are ranked separately, the first three positions for women are flexible hours, remote work and private insurance, while the order for men is remote work, flexible hours and private insurance. Training occupies fourth place for men but fifth for women, ahead of gym membership in the latter ranking.
Because each employee could select several benefits, the combined figures do not indicate the number of individual employees in either gender group. The chart therefore supports comparisons between benefit preferences, but it cannot be used to calculate the percentage of employees choosing each option without knowing the sizes of the two groups.

sourceControls.correctExample: Flexible hours were selected by women from a list of six benefits.

sourceControls.correctExample: The figure was higher by 20 but included fewer than 30 additional respondents.
sourceControls.boundaryZhHantHk: higher by 描述數值差；fewer 修飾可數名詞。

sourceControls.boundaryZhHantHk: 類別可主動 record 數值；人可主動 select 類別。

sourceControls.correctExample: The total was 560, and the category recorded a total of 560 selections.
sourceControls.boundaryZhHantHk: 表語數值不用 of；名詞結構 a total of 需要 of。

sourceControls.correctExample: The figures were close to each other, with the male figure 40 higher.
sourceControls.boundaryZhHantHk: close to 是固定結構；with 可接省略式名詞補語。

sourceControls.correctExample: As many as 280 women participated, but as much as £280 was spent.
sourceControls.boundaryZhHantHk: 可數名詞用 many；不可數金額用 much。

sourceControls.correctExample: The female figure was three times the male figure. It was 200 per cent higher than the male figure.
sourceControls.boundaryZhHantHk: three times as high 與 200% higher 等值；避免含糊的 three times higher。

sourceControls.correctExample: Women made up three quarters of the total, while men accounted for one quarter.
sourceControls.boundaryZhHantHk: make up 和 account for 都可表示構成比例。

sourceControls.correctExample: Childcare ranked fourth, or it occupied fourth place.
sourceControls.boundaryZhHantHk: rank fourth 和 occupy fourth place 均不用 the。

sourceControls.correctExample: Gym membership showed a male advantage and was advantageous for male employees.
sourceControls.boundaryZhHantHk: 名詞 advantage 與形容詞 advantageous 的不同結構。

sourceControls.correctExample: A total of 250 men participated. The total number of men was 250.
sourceControls.boundaryZhHantHk: a total of 與 the total number of 都正確。

sourceControls.correctExample: There were 80 fewer women than men, and the female figure was 80 lower.
sourceControls.boundaryZhHantHk: fewer 修飾人數；lower 描述數值。

sourceControls.correctExample: The number of men was one and a half times that of women.
sourceControls.boundaryZhHantHk: number 為單數，省略時使用 that。

sourceControls.correctExample: Gym membership was less popular, although fewer employees selected it.
sourceControls.boundaryZhHantHk: less 修飾形容詞；fewer 修飾複數名詞。

sourceControls.correctExample: Women made 1,830 selections, but they did not make 1,830 individual visits.
sourceControls.boundaryZhHantHk: make selections 是固定搭配；同一人可以作多項選擇。

sourceControls.correctExample: The women's total was 80 higher than the men's.
sourceControls.boundaryZhHantHk: 所有格可省略重複的名詞 total。

sourceControls.correctExample: Together, the two categories accounted for one third of the total.
sourceControls.boundaryZhHantHk: account for 與分數 of the total。

sourceControls.correctExample: Two fifths of the selections were made by men, but one fifth was made by women.

sourceControls.correctExample: The categories were ranked separately, but the overall totals were compared together.

sourceControls.correctExample: Of the two rankings, the former was for men and the latter for women.
sourceControls.boundaryZhHantHk: former/latter 僅適用於兩個已按次序提及的項目。

sourceControls.correctExample: Each employee selected several benefits, and all employees selected at least one.
sourceControls.boundaryZhHantHk: each + 單數；all + 複數。

sourceControls.correctExample: Neither group selected the option. The total did not identify employees in either group.

sourceControls.correctExample: The chart shows selection counts, not percentages of individual employees.
